title: Ang 1035: before creation
hook: for countless ages there was only darkness and the Formless (Maru Solhe M1, ang 1035)
tomorrow: how do you stop freezing when every face turns to you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Solhe: sixteen stanzas, and two ways in, the sound and the sense. Today one of those long hymns goes somewhere nobody has been.

When the power cuts out at night, there's a second of real dark. The fridge stops humming. The router light dies. Your eyes reach for something and find nothing. A hand goes straight for a phone flashlight. Guru Nanak, in one of his Maru Solhe on ang 1035, stays in that dark on purpose, and goes further back than any blackout: to before there was a world to light.
screen: `THE POWER CUTS OUT.` → `THE HUM STOPS.` → `FURTHER BACK THAN ANY BLACKOUT.`

segments.voice: The hymn opens, in paraphrase: for endless ages there was only utter darkness. No earth, no sky, only the infinite hukam, the order of the One. No day, no night, no moon, no sun. The Formless sat in sunn samadh, a deep, absorbed stillness. Then it keeps taking things away: no speech, no air, no water, no being born, no dying, no coming and going. Listen to how it's built. Almost every line is a no. The hymn makes you feel the empty space by removing each thing you'd normally lean on. And yet it's never quite empty. Something is there in every line: the hukam, the One, absorbed and still. The dark isn't nothing. It's full, before anything has a shape. Later in the hymn the turn comes, again in paraphrase: when it pleased the One, the world was made. Light, sky and earth arrive only then, as a choice, not an accident. So the dark at the start of the hymn isn't scary. It's the room before the lights come on, and someone is already in it. Before the beginning.
screen: `ONLY DARKNESS, ONLY HUKAM.` · `NO SUN, NO MOON, NO WORDS.` · `NEVER QUITE EMPTY.` · `WHEN IT PLEASED, THE WORLD.` · then, large: `BEFORE THE BEGINNING.`

segments.voice: Rub your palms together until they're warm, then cup them gently over closed eyes so the dark is complete. Stay in that dark and notice it isn't empty: there's breath, a heartbeat, the warmth of your own hands. Near the end of the sit, lower your hands and let the light come back slowly.
Ang 1035. Where Guru Nanak's Maru Solha goes back before creation: only darkness, and the hukam of the Formless.
Carry it: before the beginning, the dark was already full. Fifteen-seventy-two, lights coming back on.

screen: `DAY 1572 COUNTS.` → `A WALK THROUGH THE GRANTH · 126 OF 180.` → `TOMORROW: HOW DO YOU STOP FREEZING?`

howItsDone: Guru Nanak's Maru Solha on ang 1035, describing the time before creation, is sung in kirtan and often explained in katha as the Granth's account of what was there before the world.

fork.setup: your friend's grandmother has died, and your friend says the silence in the house is unbearable, like nothing is left. which picture from ang 1035 might a Sikh friend offer gently?
options: the dark before creation wasn't empty; the One was already there.
silence means God has gone away until the noise comes back.
you should fill the house with sound so you never feel it.
fork.reveal: Guru Nanak's hymn takes everything away, sun, moon, speech, and still the hukam and the Formless are there. the stillness is full.

original.note: Gurmukhi: dhundhukaara, utter darkness; Guru Nanak's word for before creation (ang 1035).

chat.says: fateh slept over. since the patka thing he wants every light on. how do i help him w the dark
options: Sit with him in it. Guru Nanak says even before the world, the dark wasn't empty.
Tell him the hymn says the dark is just nothing, so there's nothing in it to fear.
Leave the lights on. The hymn says God only came once the light was made.
chat.meaning: On ang 1035 everything is taken away, sun, moon, speech, and still the hukam and the Formless are there. The dark is full.

hukam.meaning: the order or will of the One

sunn samadh.meaning: deep, absorbed stillness, as in a trance

Solha.meaning: one of the Solhe, a single long hymn
